Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

pension noun

also pensions, pensioner, state pension, old-age pension, retirement pay, social security

classical

Suet. Tib. 50.1: praebitīsque annuīs fraudāvit, he cheated her of the yearly payments
Plin. Ep. 10.31.2: ut pūblicī servī annua accipiunt, they draw a yearly allowance like public slaves

annua, annuōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

a yearly allowance; a pension

Money paid every year: an annuity, a stipend, a pension (Lewis & Short); Nero granted impoverished senators annua salāria (Suet. Ner. 10.1). Not pēnsiō, which is classically a payment or rent (see rent, money paid for a house or flat).

Other words

  • commoda missiōnum — a soldier’s benefits on discharge

    noun and genitive · also used · classical · Suet. Aug. 49.2: dēfīnītīs … commodīs missiōnum; Suet. Ner. 32.1: commoda veterānōrum, the veterans’ benefits

    Augustus fixed them by rank and years of service and set up a fund to pay them (see fund): the nearest classical thing to a pension.

  • beneficium annuum — a pension

    noun and adjective · also used · modern · Levi–Bini p. 47: beneficium annuum tribuere, to pension someone off

  • beneficiārius, beneficiāriī m. — a pensioner (Levi–Bini)

    noun, second declension · avoid · modern · Levi–Bini p. 47 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically a soldier excused fatigues by his commander’s favour, often his orderly (Caes. BC 1.75; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Quidquid autem ubīque mīlitum esset, ad certam stīpendiōrum praemiōrumque fōrmulam adstrīnxit dēfīnītīs prō gradū cujusque et temporibus mīlitiae et commodīs missiōnum, nē aut aetāte aut inopiā post missiōnem sollicitārī ad rēs novās possent.

    All the soldiers everywhere he bound to a fixed scale of pay and rewards, setting for each rank both the years of service and the benefits on discharge, so that neither age nor want should tempt them to revolution once they had left the army.Suet. Aug. 49.2

  • sed et pecūliō concessō ā patre praebitīsque annuīs fraudāvit

    and he even cheated her of the allowance her father had granted her and of the yearly payments he had providedSuet. Tib. 50.1

  • assēcūrātiō sociālis

    social securityTraupman 382

See also retire, salary, fund, income.
